meta.sponsor: Merck (funder); University of Oxford CTSU (regulatory sponsor) with TIMI Study Group
meta.indication: secondary prevention in atherosclerotic vascular disease on intensive atorvastatin

n_randomized.quote: We conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 30,449 adults with atherosclerotic vascular disease who were receiving intensive atorvastatin therapy

median_followup.quote: During the median follow-up period of 4.1 years, the primary outcome occurred in significantly fewer patients in the anacetrapib group than in the placebo group

primary_endpoint.value: First major coronary event: coronary death, myocardial infarction, or coronary revascularization
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary outcome was the first major coronary event, a composite of coronary death, myocardial infarction, or coronary revascularization.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age >50 y with history of MI, cerebrovascular atherosclerotic disease, PAD, or diabetes with symptomatic CHD; run-in on protocol atorvastatin (mean LDL-C 61 mg/dL at randomization)
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Men and women older than 50 years were considered eligible if they met at least one of the inclusion criteria (history of MI, cerebrovascular atherosclerotic disease, peripheral arterial disease, or diabetes mellitus with other evidence of symptomatic coronary heart disease)

planned_events.quote: Follow-up of all randomized participants is planned to continue for a median of at least 4 years, and until at least 1900 participants have had an unrefuted major coronary event (primary end point) plus at least 950 participants have had a coronary death or MI.
planned_events.note: Minimum target; 3443 primary events actually occurred (1640 + 1803).

assumed_rrr.quote: We assumed an annual rate of major coronary events of 1.8% in the placebo group and determined that a sample size of 30,000 patients with a median follow-up of 4 years would provide the trial with a power of 88% at a two-tailed P value of less than 0.01 (and 96% power at P<0.05) to detect a 15% lower risk of major coronary events in the anacetrapib group than in the placebo group.
assumed_rrr.note: Design paper S2 states the same 88%/P<.01/15%.

power.quote: a power of 88% at a two-tailed P value of less than 0.01 (and 96% power at P<0.05)
power.note: Design paper (Feb 2017), using the observed blinded event rate of 2.7%/y, projected 98% power at P<.01 for 15% RRR.

alpha.quote: a power of 88% at a two-tailed P value of less than 0.01
alpha.note: 0.01 is the alpha used for the power calculation; design paper: 'A 2-tailed P value <.05 will be considered statistically significant.'

stopped_early.quote: In November 2015, the DMC considered the guidelines for premature stopping (see Supplementary Material) and recommended that the study continue as planned.
stopped_early.note: Ran to scheduled completion; registry: all participants stopped study treatment prior to February 2017, primary completion 2017-01-31.

baseline.quote: a mean LDL cholesterol level of 61 mg per deciliter (1.58 mmol per liter)
a mean non-HDL cholesterol level of 92 mg per deciliter (2.38 mmol per liter)
a mean HDL cholesterol level of 40 mg per deciliter (1.03 mmol per liter)

biomarker_effects.quote: At the trial midpoint, the mean level of HDL cholesterol was higher by 43 mg per deciliter (1.12 mmol per liter) in the anacetrapib group than in the placebo group (a relative difference of 104%)
the mean level of non-HDL cholesterol was lower by 17 mg per deciliter (0.44 mmol per liter), a relative difference of −18%
biomarker_effects.note: Merck release S5 states the same.

biomarker_effects.quote: lower by 11 mg per deciliter (0.28 mmol per liter) as measured on beta quantification in a randomly selected subgroup of 2000 patients, a relative difference of −17% (Table 2)

The mean LDL cholesterol level was lower by 26 mg per deciliter (0.68 mmol per liter) in the anacetrapib group than in the placebo group as measured on a direct assay (which underestimates the LDL cholesterol level among patients treated with anacetrapib16), a relative difference of −41%
the mean level of apolipoprotein B was lower by 12 mg per deciliter (0.12 g per liter, a relative difference of −18%)
The mean level of apolipoprotein A1 was higher by 42 mg per deciliter (0.42 g per liter) in the anacetrapib group than in the placebo group (a relative difference of 36%)
the mean level of lipoprotein(a) was lower by 15 nmol per liter (a relative difference of −25%)
a 39.8% reduction with anacetrapib beyond that seen with placebo
biomarker_effects.note: DEFINE methods: 'LDL cholesterol levels were calculated with the use of the Friedewald equation'. Friedewald/direct methods underestimate LDL-C on anacetrapib vs beta-quantification by ~10-12 mg/dL (S8).

biomarker_effects.quote: a 138.1% increase with anacetrapib beyond that seen with placebo
In the anacetrapib group, apolipoprotein B levels decreased by 21.0% and apolipoprotein A-I levels increased by 44.7% beyond the changes seen in the placebo group (P<0.001) (Table 2).

Treatment with anacetrapib was associated with a 31.7% reduction in non-HDL cholesterol, a 36.4% reduction in lipoprotein(a) levels, and a 6.8% reduction in triglyceride levels, beyond the changes seen in the placebo group.

For placebo and anacetrapib monotherapy (10, 40, 150, and 300 mg), least squares mean percent changes from baseline to week 8 for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) were 2%, -16%, -27%, -40%, and -39%, respectively, and for HDL-C were 4%, 44%, 86%, 139%, and 133%, respectively
biomarker_effects.note: From-baseline; placebo +2%. 100 mg dose (used in REVEAL) not tested here.

hr.quote: rate ratio, 0.91; 95% confidence interval, 0.85 to 0.97; P=0.004
hr.note: Log-rank rate ratio. Registry S3 identical.

safety_signals.quote: with higher levels of systolic blood pressure (by 0.7 mm Hg) and diastolic blood pressure (by 0.3 mm Hg) at the final visit. However, there was no significant difference in the rates of serious adverse events attributed to hypertension (1.0% in the anacetrapib group vs. 0.9% in the placebo group)

safety_signals.value: eGFR <60 at end of study 11.5% vs 10.6%
safety_signals.quote: more patients in the anacetrapib group developed an estimated glomerular filtration rate of less than 60 ml/min/1.73m 2 by the end of the study (11.5% vs. 10.6%; P=0.04)

safety_signals.value: Accumulation of anacetrapib in adipose tissue with prolonged dosing
safety_signals.quote: The safety profile of anacetrapib in the early analysis was generally consistent with that demonstrated in previous studies of the drug, including accumulation of anacetrapib in adipose tissue, as has been previously reported.

safety_signals.value: No excess death, cancer or other serious adverse events
safety_signals.quote: There were no significant between-group differences in the risk of death, cancer, or other serious adverse events.

safety_signals.value: Key secondary (major atherosclerotic events) not significant; no effect on presumed ischemic stroke
safety_signals.note: Registry S3: 1383 vs 1483, RR 0.93 (0.86-1.00); ischemic stroke 485 vs 489, RR 0.99.

genetics.finding: Common CETP variants (TaqIB, I405V, -629C>A) that modestly lower CETP activity and raise HDL-C are weakly associated with lower coronary risk (meta-analysis, 27,196 cases).
genetics.effect: per-allele OR for coronary disease 0.95 (0.92-0.99) for TaqIB
genetics.quote: The combined per-allele odds ratios (ORs) for coronary disease were 0.95 (95% CI, 0.92-0.99) for TaqIB, 0.94 (95% CI, 0.89-1.00) for I405V, and 0.95 (95% CI, 0.91-1.00) for -629C>A.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: genetically raised HDL-C (LIPG Asn396Ser; 14-SNP HDL score) does not lower MI risk; LDL score does.
genetics.effect: LIPG 396Ser OR 0.99 (0.88-1.11); HDL genetic score OR per 1 SD 0.93 (0.68-1.26)
genetics.quote: However, a 1 SD increase in HDL cholesterol due to genetic score was not associated with risk of myocardial infarction (OR 0·93, 95% CI 0·68-1·26, p=0·63).

genetics.finding: Rare CETP protein-truncating variants (1 in 975 carriers) raise HDL-C, lower LDL-C and triglycerides, and are associated with lower CHD risk.
genetics.quote: CETP PTV carrier status was associated with reduced risk for CHD (summary odds ratio, 0.70; 95% confidence interval, 0.54-0.90; P=5.1×10-3).

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: CETP genetic score lowers CV risk in proportion to apoB reduction; on a statin (HMGCR) background the apoB reduction and the risk reduction are attenuated, so benefit tracks apoB, not LDL-C or HDL-C.
genetics.effect: CETP score alone OR 0.946 (0.921-0.972); combined with HMGCR score OR 0.985 (0.955-1.015)
genetics.quote: When combined with the HMGCR score, the CETP score was associated with the same reduction in LDL-C levels but an attenuated reduction in apoB levels and a corresponding attenuated nonsignificant risk of major cardiovascular events (OR, 0.985 [95% CI, 0.955-1.015]).

consensus_explanation.summary: Anacetrapib lowered non-HDL-C by 17 mg/dL (18%) and apoB by 18% on top of intensive atorvastatin and reduced major coronary events by 9%, a size consistent with the reduction in non-HDL-C/apoB (CTT-type relationship) rather than the 104% HDL-C rise. Accepted explanation: benefit of CETP inhibition is driven by lowering apoB-containing lipoproteins (Ference 2017 MR), and REVEAL succeeded where torcetrapib, dalcetrapib and evacetrapib failed because of relative safety, potency, and adequate size (30,449) and duration (4.1 y) (Tall & Rader). The modest effect, adipose accumulation and small renal/BP signals led Merck not to file. Direct LDL-C assays overstated LDL lowering (-41% direct vs -17% by beta-quantification).

pre_readout.note: readout_date 2017-06-27 (Merck topline: met primary endpoint). Full data 2017-08-29 (ESC + NEJM).
available_before_readout: Design and baseline paper (S2, online 2017-02-21, PMC open): N 30,449, 88% power at P<0.01 for 15% RRR, >=1900 events, baseline LDL 61/HDL 40, DEFINE lipid effects, beta-quantification caveat
Phase 2 DEFINE (S6, 2010-11-17): LDL-C -39.8% (Friedewald), HDL-C +138.1%, apoB -21.0%, non-HDL -31.7%, no BP/aldosterone effect
Phase 2 dose-ranging (S7, 2008-12-20): LDL-C -16 to -40%, HDL-C +44 to +139%, no BP increase
Genetics: Thompson 2008 (S11), Voight 2012 (S10), Nomura 2017-05-15 CETP PTV protective (S12)
Class evidence: ILLUMINATE, dal-OUTCOMES, ACCELERATE failures
only_after_readout: Phase 3 HR 0.91, events, apoB -18%, LDL-C -17% by beta-quantification (S1/S5, 2017-08-28/29)

access_summary.note: Key numbers (17): N, median f/u, planned events, RRR, power, alpha, HR, CI low, CI high, p, events T, events C, phase-3 HDL-C, non-HDL-C, LDL-C (beta-quant), apoB, readout date. Each counted once at the most accessible place. abstract_only (free NEJM abstract on PubMed/Europe PMC) = N, f/u, HR, CIs, p, events T/C, HDL-C, non-HDL-C (10); most are also in the registry and Merck release. open_full_text = planned events, RRR, power, alpha (design paper, PMC open access) + LDL-C by beta-quantification and apoB (NEJM full text only: free in a browser, 403 to scripts) (6). press = readout date (1).

Power: NEJM 88% at P<0.01 (96% at P<0.05); design paper (Feb 2017) projected 98% at P<0.01 using the observed 2.7%/y event rate.
Planned events: design paper says 'at least 1900' primary events; 3443 actually accrued. No single fixed event target.
